since_text: A quiet day. One airplane came on: a 1955 Cessna 180, N4798B, at $140,000 in Wasilla, Alaska, posted on Craigslist yesterday by its owner — P-Ponk 470, 29-inch Bushwheels, new panel and interior, floats that need work and a set of penetration skis thrown in, and the ad's own words are 'very little damage history'; the tail was read off the photograph and the public record for that serial holds a 1972 NTSB entry marked destroyed and a 1980 substantial one. One airplane went: C-GGKA, the 1979 A185F amphibian at $280,000 at Mill Bay, British Columbia, whose only advertisement on Barnstormers now says the ad is not presently available, and which is on no other site or group. Not one asking price moved on any primary site. Three figures look different without moving: Controller's for-sale page for N53044, the 650-hour 1973 A185F amphibian from Wipaire, reads 'Under Contract' and 'Call for price' again while Trade-A-Plane and a fresh Barnstormers re-post of 14 October both print $520,000; C-GLCQ in St John's is CA$290,000 and Controller's US-dollar rendering drifts a few hundred dollars a day with the exchange rate; and ZS-FNF's R4.75 million is converted to $360,000 by one site and $294,970 by another. Two identities firmed up: the Waukesha 1958 180A amphibian at $130,000 is N392PT, serial 50140, printed by the seller in a group card, and its public record holds a 2005 nose-over and a 2013 gear incident; the Norway 1981 185F is LN-NFD, read off its photo. The UK 1979 A185F at £325,000 now has its post date, 13 September, and its hours, 4,263. Nine photographs were added; eight Barnstormers-only ads were confirmed to carry no photograph at all. Three aircraft were not seen anywhere today and stay on the record with a flag: N4757Q and N70713 for the second run, and the Turner, Montana 1978 180 for the first. Turned away after reading them: a 1982 185F at $350,000 in north-eastern Wyoming and a 1980 A185F amphibian at $395,000 at Pontiac, Michigan, both group posts older than sixty days; two Flybuyer airplanes, a 1965 185D at $215,000 and a 1975 185F at $289,000, both marked sold on Marketplace; a 1966 180H at CA$199,000 in the BC Rockies whose Barnstormers ad is gone and whose group post is from May; a 1976 A185F, N28JE, at $290,000 on AvPay whose broker's own site no longer lists it; a 1978 180K, N66566, at $325,000 in Montana whose Controller ad now redirects to the search page; and two Skywagons airplanes on sprinkle.com, a 1968 180H and a 1974 180, that are not in the dealer's own inventory.
provenance: Every source was reached. Controller, GlobalAir and AvPay were read from the cloud side through the search tool's links; everything else, and every photograph, came through the browser pane on the Mac mini, which answered at 11:10 UTC and was signed in to Facebook throughout with no sign-in wall. Facebook Marketplace was searched at fourteen cities with four terms each and holds to about forty miles of each city; twenty-eight Facebook groups were searched with four terms each, 112 passes, and every candidate post was opened to read its date. aerogurus, FindAircraft and sprinkle.com repeat inventory other sites have sold, so nothing enters from them unless a primary advertisement confirms it. Three listings were not re-sighted this run and are flagged on the row rather than dropped; a listing leaves the record only when its advertisement is gone or after seven consecutive unsighted runs with no ad page.

The windscreen and all windows (including bubble side windows) were replaced when the aircraft was repainted in 2002, the paint & interior still show very well. Float kit "Option A" installed with almost new WIP 3,000s. Owner moved out of state to care for elderly loved ones, but engine was preserved before he left. Reason for selling - no longer in Alaska & decided someone else should enjoy it like he did. If doesn't sell, will relocate to lower 48 & keep flying.
